svg.title: N-grams shorten history so we can count
svg.desc: The exact chain rule conditions each word on its entire preceding history. N-gram models apply an (N−1)-order Markov assumption, using only the last N−1 words; shorter histories repeat more often in a corpus but lose context.

g.text: N-grams shorten history so we can count
The chain rule is exact; the Markov assumption trades context for repeated evidence.
Target next word: “begun” · preceding sentence: “The monsoon season has begun”
Shorter context → more repeated counts, but less information about the sentence.
